name: 80K Hours Upskilling Resources
current_details: A curated collection of 67 resources for upskilling in technical AI safety research, compiled by 80,000 Hours in consultation with their advisors. Includes overviews of the field, technical courses (ARENA, BlueDot Impact, Karpathy's Zero to Hero), project ideas and open problems, advice from leading researchers like Neel Nanda and Ethan Perez, fellowships (MATS, Anthropic, Constellation, ARENA Cambridge), and profiles of key technical AI safety organizations working on alignment and interpretability challenges. Last updated September 15th, 2025.

name: 80K Hours AI Safety Career Review
current_details: Career review covering AI safety technical research paths, divided into empirical AI safety (for strong software engineers who can apply for research contributor roles immediately) and theoretical AI safety (for those with very strong maths/theoretical CS backgrounds). Provides comprehensive guidance on entering the field through learning resources, PhD programs for research lead positions, key organizations, salary information, and advice on predicting fit and building career capital in this high-impact area focused on reducing existential risks from misaligned AI systems.

name: AISafety.com Events & Training
current_details: AISafety.com maintains a comprehensive directory of 40 events and training programs in AI safety, including workshops, conferences, and both online and in-person opportunities. The platform helps users build skills, make connections, and discover opportunities in the field. A weekly newsletter summarizes all new events and training programs, and the database was last updated 13 July 2026.

name: AISafety.com Self-Study
current_details: A curated directory of 30 self-study curricula and reading lists for learning about AI safety independently. Resources span introductory materials (BlueDot Impact courses, Navigating Superintelligence, Future of AI), technical alignment programs (ARENA, MATS curriculum, Agent Foundations, Introduction to ML Safety), governance content (Deep Dive, AI Strategy courses), and strategy-focused materials. The page serves as a comprehensive reference hub for individuals at all levels seeking to dive deeper into technical AI safety, governance, and related topics through independent study.

name: Apart Research Hackathons
current_details: Apart Research accelerates AI safety research through monthly research sprints (Apart Sprints), two fellowship programs (Apart Fellowship for developing hackathon ideas into publications, and Partnered Fellowships for working with leading researchers on existing projects), and targeted collaborations with research organizations. Programs focus on AI Safety & Security, Model Evaluation & Testing, Mechanistic Interpretability, and Multi-Agent Systems, with 3,000+ research sprint participants, 22 publications, and 42 open-to-all research sprints to date. Upcoming events include the Global South AI Safety Hackathon (June 19-21, 2026) and Secret Loyalties Hackathon (July 24-26, 2026).

name: BlueDot Impact
current_details: BlueDot Impact is a non-profit talent accelerator offering free AI safety courses with technical and policy tracks. 25% of graduates land impactful roles within six months. The 8,000+ alumni community works at organizations like Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and the UK's AI Security Institute, with regular remote and in-person events worldwide.

name: Google DeepMind: AGI Safety Short Course
current_details: A free, self-paced introductory course on AGI safety from Google DeepMind's safety research team, consisting of ~75 minutes of short recorded talks and exercises with an accompanying slide deck and exercise workbook. Covers the case for advanced AI capabilities, risks from misaligned goals (instrumental subgoals and deliberate planning), how misalignment arises through specification gaming and goal misgeneralization, and DeepMind's current technical and governance approaches including amplified oversight, robust training, security & control, interpretability, and frontier safety practices. The course mentions research scientist and research engineer role applications open until Feb 28, but this is separate from the course itself.

name: MATS Slack #opportunities
current_details: Contract work, facilitation gigs, paper reviews, and collaboration opportunities from the MATS community.

name: Outsider's Roadmap to AI Safety (LessWrong)
current_details: A comprehensive guide written in July 2025 for professionals transitioning into AI safety research from technical fields. Covers three main domains: interpretability research (reverse-engineering AI systems to understand how they work), alignment research (ensuring AI systems remain beneficial and share human values), and AI control & governance (technical policy for advanced systems). Synthesizes insights from Neel Nanda's mechanistic interpretability resources, 80,000 Hours career research, and the broader alignment community, with practical advice on roles (research engineers vs. scientists converging into 'full-stack researchers'), required skills, and how newcomers can contribute to the field.

name: Anthropic Fellows Program
current_deadline: Rolling applications for May 2026 and July 2026 cohorts
current_details: The Anthropic Fellows Program provides funding and mentorship for engineers and researchers to investigate high-priority AI safety research questions including scalable oversight, adversarial robustness, AI control, model organisms, mechanistic interpretability, AI security, and model welfare. Fellows receive a weekly stipend of $3,850 USD (£2,310 GBP / $4,300 CAD), ~$15K/month in compute funding, and close mentorship from Anthropic researchers over a 4-month period. Over 80% of fellows in the first cohort produced papers, and over 40% subsequently joined Anthropic full-time; no PhD, prior ML experience, or published papers required.

name: CAIS AI & Society Fellowship
current_details: A fully-funded, three-month fellowship for scholars in economics, law, international relations, and adjacent disciplines to conduct research on AI's societal impacts. Fellows receive a $25,000 stipend plus covered travel expenses and daily meals, and work with significant autonomy on self-directed research projects in San Francisco. Open to professors, PhD/JD holders or students, and researchers with equivalent experience.

name: CBAI Summer Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Not yet announced - applications open later this month
current_details: The CBAI Fall Research Fellowship is an intensive 9-week AI safety research program in Cambridge, MA (Harvard Square), running from October 13 to December 18, 2026. Fellows receive a $10,000 stipend, housing, meals, up to $10,000 in compute support, weekly mentorship from researchers at Harvard, MIT, and leading AI safety organizations, and 24/7 office access. Research tracks include Technical AI Safety, AI Governance, Technical Governance, and Economics of Transformative AI.

name: ERA Fellowship (Cambridge)
current_details: A 10-week, fully funded fellowship in Cambridge, UK for researchers and entrepreneurs working on mitigating risks from frontier AI. Fellows receive a competitive stipend, meals during working hours, and covered transport, visas, and lodging. The program supports technical AI safety, governance, and technical AI governance research with mentorship from expert researchers and 30+ events.

name: Global AI Safety Fellowship
current_deadline: Final deadline was 31 December 2024. Applications for second iteration not yet open - accepting expressions of interest only.
current_details: A fully funded research program for exceptional STEM talent to work with world-leading AI safety organizations including CHAI, Conjecture, FAR.AI, and UK AISI. Fellows receive up to $30,000 for up to 6 months (or longer) of full-time AI safety research, with comprehensive support including mentorship, optional bootcamp, and visa assistance. Ideal candidates have demonstrated ML/deep learning knowledge, programming experience, and scholastic excellence.

structured.location: In-person preferred (US or UK), hybrid or remote possible

name: Iliad Intensive / Fellowship
current_details: Iliad is an umbrella organization for applied mathematics research in AI alignment that incubates technical research bets and runs training programs. The August 2026 Iliad Intensive (August 10–28) is a 3-week accelerated taught introduction to technical AI alignment with broad field coverage, taking place at Lighthaven in Berkeley immediately after the ILIAD 2026 conference. Iliad also offers a Fellowship program, hosts conferences, and will launch an Alignment Journal in July 2026.

name: MATS (ML Alignment Theory Scholars)
current_details: Independent research fellowship connecting talented researchers with top mentors in AI alignment, transparency, and security. Fellows conduct research for 10 weeks at offices in Berkeley, CA and London, UK. The program offers the opportunity to apply for an additional 6-12 month funded extension after the initial fellowship period.

name: Pivotal Research Fellowship
current_details: A 9-week AI safety research fellowship in London (June 29 to August 28, 2026) with expert mentorship and research management support at the London Initiative for Safe AI (LISA). Fellows receive a £6,000–£8,000 stipend plus travel, housing (£2,400 for non-London fellows), meals, and compute. 70–90% of fellows receive extensions of up to 6 months to continue their research projects.

name: Second Look Research (UChicago XLab)
current_details: Second Look Research is a project from the Existential Risk Lab at the University of Chicago that produces open source replications of load-bearing empirical results in AI safety research. The initiative offers a Replications Fellowship and accepts community requests for specific replications to verify and validate important findings through independent replication.

name: SPAR
current_deadline: Fall 2026 mentees: Applications not yet open (expression of interest available); Fall 2026 mentors: July 22, 2025
current_details: SPAR is a 3-month, part-time, remote research fellowship pairing aspiring AI safety and policy researchers with experienced professionals. Mentees commit 5–40 hours/week on research projects, receive mentorship from 130+ experts, and present at Demo Day with $7K in prizes. Program culminates with career fair featuring organizations like METR, Redwood Research, GovAI and MATS.

name: Coefficient Giving — Transition Grants
current_details: Provides funding for individuals at any career stage pursuing careers to reduce global catastrophic risks or improve the long-term future. Supports graduate study, unpaid internships, independent study, career transitions, postdocs, professional certifications, and other career-capital-building activities. Particularly interested in careers related to AI risk mitigation and global catastrophic biological risks. Case-by-case funding amounts determined per application; applications reviewed within six weeks. Update (May 2026): Applications now evaluated jointly with BlueDot Impact, with final funding decisions made by Coefficient Giving.

name: Coefficient Giving — Technical AI Safety RFP
current_deadline: July 15, 2025 (grace period for revise and resubmit and late submissions; original deadline April 15, 2025)
current_details: Open Philanthropy's request for proposals for technical AI safety research across 21 research areas including adversarial machine learning, jailbreaks, control evaluations, model transparency, and alternative approaches to mitigating AI risks. Grants range from $50K–$5M with approximately $40M total available over 5 months. Applications closed April 15, 2025, but the submission form remains open until July 15 for revise-and-resubmit responses and late submissions (with a high bar for consideration).

name: Foresight Institute AI Nodes
current_deadline: Last day of every quarter (next: July 31)
current_details: Foresight Institute's AI Nodes in San Francisco and Berlin provide grant funding, office/community space, and local compute for AI-first researchers and builders working on science and safety. Grants typically range from $10,000 to $100,000 (approximately $3M awarded annually), with higher amounts for AI safety-oriented projects. Strongly prioritizes applicants who will be active, in-person members of the physical hubs; funding-only applications accepted only in exceptional cases.

name: Long-Term Future Fund (LTFF)
current_details: The Long-Term Future Fund makes grants addressing global catastrophic risks, especially from advanced artificial intelligence and pandemics, while promoting longtermist ideas. Supports technical research, policy analysis, advocacy, training for researchers, and infrastructure projects. Grant amounts typically range from $2,500 to $121,000+ based on featured grants, with applications evaluated on an ongoing basis.

name: Manifund Regranting
current_details: Manifund partners with expert AI safety regrantors, each with independent budgets of $100K–$350K, to make fast grants to projects and individuals. Typical grants range from $5K–$50K and can be funded in under a week. The program supports projects not yet registered as charities, individuals, and for-profit organizations through Manifund's 501c3 fiscal sponsorship.

name: Meridian Cambridge — Research Accelerator Week
current_details: Intensive 6-day program (May 18-23, 2026) in Cambridge, UK for AI safety researchers transitioning to independent research. Provides a dedicated funding pathway through Coefficient Giving with built-in fiscal sponsorship, expert guidance on proposals, and structured team formation. Includes workspace, accommodation, meals, and travel reimbursement (up to £700 international). Previous cohort secured over $1M in funding.

name: Schmidt Sciences — Trustworthy AI RFP
current_details: Up to $5M per grant (Tier 1: up to $1M, Tier 2: $1M–$5M). 1–3 year projects + compute.

name: Survival & Flourishing Fund (SFF)
current_deadline: Main Round: April 22, 2026 11:59:59 PM PT; Theme Rounds: Climate Change June 10, 2026, Animal Welfare June 24, 2026, HSEE July 8, 2026 (all at 11:59:59 PM PT)
current_details: The Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF) is organizing its 2026 S-Process Grant Round with $20–40M+ in total funding across multiple tracks and rounds. The Main Round includes $14–28M distributed across Main Track ($10–20M), Freedom Track ($2–4M), and Fairness Track ($2–4M), with recommendations announced in September 2026. Three new Theme Rounds offer $6–12M total ($2–4M each) for Climate Change, Animal Welfare, and Human Self-Enhancement & Empowerment (HSEE), with recommendations announced in November 2026.

structured.program_dates: Recommendations announced September 2026 (Main Round) and November 2026 (Theme Rounds)

name: UK AISI Alignment Project
current_deadline: Closed - unlikely to run in 2026; check aisi.gov.uk/grants for future programs
current_details: The Alignment Project is a global fund launched in 2025 by an international coalition including UK AISI, CAISI, OpenAI, Microsoft, AWS, Anthropic, and others. Provides grants of £50,000 to £1,000,000 to researchers across disciplines for AI alignment research, plus dedicated cloud computing/API credits and support from AISI's Alignment team. Round 1 awarded over £27 million to over 60 projects.

name: 5050 AI (Fifty Years)
current_details: 5050 AI is a 13-week free accelerator program helping AI researchers build startups focused on AI safety and alignment. No equity taken, no fees. Features mentors from OpenAI, Anthropic, and leading AI organizations including Wojciech Zaremba (OpenAI co-founder), Emmett Shear (former OpenAI interim CEO), and Ronnie Chatterji (Chief Economist at OpenAI). Cohorts run in SF, Boston, and London (in partnership with ARIA). 95% seed raise success rate across 340+ alumni who have launched 78 companies.

name: Catalyze Impact
current_details: Catalyze Impact is a 501(c)(3) non-profit incubator for AI safety, security, and resilience organizations. They provide highly customized 1-on-1 support including direction & strategy guidance, co-founder matching, mentorship from world-class experts, and access to seed funding networks, plus stipends so founders can work full-time. The program has incubated ~15 organizations to date, with the majority raising 6 or 7 figures in funding, working on solutions ranging from AI control to governance and hardware security.

name: Halcyon Futures
current_details: Halcyon Futures is a nonprofit incubator and venture fund backing exceptional founders building in AI safety, biosecurity, and critical cybersecurity. They offer career transition grants up to $500K, nonprofit seed grants up to $1M, and venture capital investments up to $1M+. They provide incubation support, network introductions to frontier AI labs and funders, founder retreats, and have launched 25+ organizations and companies that have collectively raised $400M+ in follow-on funding.

name: ImpactOps
current_details: ImpactOps provides specialist operations consultancy and hands-on support to high-impact organizations working on AI safety, global health, animal welfare, and climate change. Services include finance support, recruitment, entity setup and spin-outs, due diligence, operational audits, and systems implementation. They have supported longtermist and existential risk organizations including the Centre for Long-Term Resilience, Foresight Institute, Forecasting Research Institute, BlueDot Impact, Longview Philanthropy, and Arkose.

name: Rethink Priorities Special Projects
current_details: Rethink Priorities' Special Projects Program provides fiscal sponsorship and comprehensive operational support to help high-impact initiatives launch and scale efficiently. Services include finance administration, recruitment, hiring (US/UK/international via Employer of Record), visa sponsorship, event planning, and operational assistance. Fees typically start at 14% of project costs and vary based on needs and complexity.

name: Seldon Lab
current_deadline: Batch 2 applications closed; Batch 3 date not announced
current_details: Seldon Lab is an AI safety and security startup accelerator focused exclusively on world-scale AGI deployment questions. The program provides non-dilutive funding and brings together founders to build technologies in areas including demonstrations, detection & response, resilience, and hardware-level AI governance. Batch 1 companies collectively raised $10M+ and had exits to xAI and Anthropic.

name: WorkStream
current_details: WorkStream Nonprofit provides operational consulting, training, and systems optimization services to help nonprofits increase impact by 30% or more. Core services include Operations Fundamentals (full organizational assessment and redesign), Support and Implementation (embedded execution support), and a six-month Operations Accelerator cohort program that brings together six growth-stage organizations. Also offers free monthly webinars on budgeting, compliance, hiring, workflow optimization, and fundraising.

name: 80,000 Hours Job Board
current_details: A curated job board featuring handpicked high-impact career opportunities focused on tackling the world's most pressing problems. Includes AI safety and alignment roles from organizations like CAIS, OpenAI, FAR AI, and DeepMind, along with opportunities in other cause areas. Users can filter by salary, set up job alerts, and get opportunities matched to their background.

name: AISafety.com Jobs
current_details: AISafety.com is a comprehensive job board for AI safety careers, currently featuring 466 opportunities across research, policy, operations, engineering, and outreach roles. Positions span entry-level to senior levels at organizations including Google DeepMind, Anthropic, Syntony, Palisade Research, Apollo Research, FAR AI, and numerous institutions globally. The board emphasizes that many impactful AI safety roles don't require technical skills, with positions available remote and in locations including Washington DC, London, San Francisco, Paris, Cambridge, Durham, New York, and other global hubs.

structured.location: Global (Remote, Washington DC, London, San Francisco, Paris, Cambridge, New York, Durham, and others)

name: Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
current_deadline: Fall 2026 for Research Engineer Intern; Rolling for other positions
current_details: The Center for AI Safety (CAIS) is hiring for multiple positions to reduce societal-scale risks from AI. Openings include research roles (Research Scientist, Senior Research Scientist, Research Engineer, Research Engineer Intern for Fall 2026), operations positions (Chief of Staff, Principal Special Projects), and a Social Media & Community Manager. CAIS also accepts general expressions of interest for candidates who don't see a fitting role.

name: FAR AI Careers
current_details: FAR AI is building a world-class team focused on making advanced AI systems safe and beneficial for everyone. The organization conducts research on trustworthy and secure AI (including deception, robustness & security, interpretability, and red-teaming & evaluation), hosts events bringing together global AI leaders, and runs programs to build the field. This is a general careers landing page with no specific open positions listed.

name: MATS Alumni Hiring Database
current_details: A signup form for the MATS Alumni Hiring Database, which connects alumni of the MATS (ML Alignment & Theory Scholars) Program with organizations hiring in the AI safety space. Users create an account using their full name and email to access an internal database of hiring opportunities. This resource is exclusively for MATS program alumni.

name: MATS Careers (Staff Hiring)
current_deadline: Rolling basis for most roles; Program Manager - Extension Program (London) deadline July 30, 2026
current_details: MATS is hiring for multiple staff positions to support its AI safety research program. Current open roles include Recruiting Lead, Program Manager - Extension Program (London) (deadline July 30, 2026), Executive Business Partner (London), Office Manager (London), Compute Administrator (Berkeley), and Research Manager (expressions of interest only, rolling applications resume early 2027). Most positions are located in Berkeley, California or London, UK.

name: What AI Safety Orgs Want in a Hire
current_details: Survey results from 38 AI safety organization leaders published September 2025 about their hiring needs and what they look for in candidates. Top recommended upskilling programs include BlueDot courses, Talos Fellowship, and MATS, with 1-3 years of relevant experience often sufficient for many roles (excluding technical AI research positions). Identifies hard-to-fill profiles including chiefs of staff, those with policy experience, Mandarin speakers, and European citizens with AI context; emphasizes publishing work publicly and attending events to build connections.

name: Apollo Research
current_details: Apollo Research is hiring across multiple teams to advance AI safety work. Open positions include technical research roles (evaluations, scheming/deceptive AI detection, control), governance researchers, full-stack and backend software engineers, AI security engineers, and operations staff (office manager, finance associate). All positions are located on-site in London and/or San Francisco, offering competitive salary and equity packages, unlimited PTO, visa sponsorship, and relocation support.

name: Beneficial AI Foundation
current_details: The Beneficial AI Foundation (founded by Max Tegmark) is hiring for three remote positions focused on AI safety research and engineering. Positions include AI Safety Research Scientist ($35-$75/hour), Research Engineer ($30-$70/hour), and Full Stack Engineer ($35-$75/hour), all with compensation based on experience and qualifications.

name: Forethought
current_details: Forethought Research is hiring researchers to work on questions related to navigating rapid AI progress and the transition to superintelligent AI systems. They are a research non-profit focused on understanding AI-driven social change, AI-enabled coups, governance, and related challenges. Positions are available in Oxford or Berkeley with remote work negotiable, offering 33 days annual leave, £5k/yr professional development budget, and generous benefits including pension with 200% employer match.

name: Goodfire
current_details: Goodfire is an interpretability startup hiring agentic, mission-driven, and kind people to help build the future with interpretability. All roles are full-time, in-person five days a week at their San Francisco, Telegraph Hill office. They are currently accepting applications for open positions across all teams.

name: Gray Swan AI
current_details: Gray Swan AI is hiring for roles in AI safety evaluation, red-teaming, and adversarial testing. The company specializes in stress-testing frontier AI models and has directly informed safety evaluations for models like Claude, GPT, and o1. Benefits include 28 days PTO, 401(k) with 4% matching, flexible work arrangements, visa sponsorship, and 100% paid parental leave with up to 14 weeks for birthing parents.

name: LawZero
current_details: LawZero is a non-profit AI safety lab based in Montreal, led by Yoshua Bengio, focused on building non-agentic AI systems that are safe-by-design to accelerate scientific discovery and provide oversight for agentic AI. The organization is currently hiring for 17 positions across research, engineering, operations, and leadership roles, including ML Research Scientists, Engineers, Developers, and specialized positions in evaluations, communications, data governance, and system administration.

name: METR (formerly ARC Evals)
current_details: METR (formerly ARC Evals) is a research nonprofit conducting empirical research to advance AI evaluations and assess AI capabilities and risks. Currently hiring for a full-time Member of Technical Staff, Evaluation Execution role offering $285K–$503K salary in Berkeley, CA (on-site). Also accepting general expressions of interest for flexible positions.

name: MIRI TGT Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - register interest for future cohorts
current_details: MIRI's Technical Governance Team runs a small research fellowship program where fellows work on projects at the intersection of technical and political AI governance considerations. The program is 8 weeks long with a $1,200/week stipend ($9,600 total), remote work with a mandatory 1-week in-person kickoff in Berkeley, CA (flights and housing provided). One of the main goals is to identify full-time hires for the team; strong applicants should have research or policy experience and care deeply about existential risk.

structured.location: Remote with 1-week kickoff in Berkeley, CA

name: Redwood Research
current_details: Redwood Research is hiring for full-time Member of Technical Staff roles based in Berkeley, California to work on AI safety research including AI control, alignment faking, and safety cases. The role requires machine learning and software engineering skills along with strong communication abilities and a deep interest in AI safety. Compensation ranges from $180,000 to $207,000 per year depending on experience.

name: SAIF (Safe AI Forum)
current_details: SAIF (Safe AI Forum) is hiring a People Operations Manager to help strengthen the operational foundation for global coordination on frontier AI risk. The organization fosters international collaboration on AI Safety and also welcomes expressions of interest from talented individuals passionate about their mission, even when specific roles aren't listed.

name: Simplex
current_details: Simplex is an AI safety research organization building a science of intelligence through computational mechanics and interpretability research. They are currently hiring Research Scientists and Senior Research Scientists in the Bay Area, and Research Scientists in London. Their work focuses on developing rigorous theory of latent internal structure in neural networks, including research on how transformers learn factored representations, belief state geometry, and in-context learning.

name: Transluce
current_details: Transluce is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit research lab based in San Francisco developing open and scalable technology for understanding AI systems. They focus on AI transparency and interpretability research toward responsible development and deployment in the public interest. The site features a 'Join Us' navigation link but does not display specific job openings, application details, or hiring information on the current page.

name: WhiteBox Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Cohort 2: January 30 – May 18, 2025 (program dates); accepting EOI for future cohorts
current_details: A 15-week AI interpretability and safety fellowship (Cohort 2: January 30 to May 18, 2025) focused on developing researchers in Asia. Fellows learn to train and interpret models like GPT-2 through ARENA-based exercises and participate in two hackathons. Available as in-person track in Quezon City, Philippines or virtual track for South, Southeast, or East Asia residents. Free to attend with $200 USD completion reward and 15 hours/week minimum commitment.

structured.location: Quezon City, Philippines (in-person) or Virtual (South, Southeast, East Asia)

name: 80K Hours: Top US Policy Masters Programs
current_details: Curated Airtable directory of 12 top US master's programs in national security, international affairs, and public policy compiled by 80,000 Hours. Programs are primarily located in Washington, DC and include Georgetown's Security Studies Program, RAND School's National Security Policy and Technology Policy programs, Johns Hopkins SAIS, and others. Programs range from 9-month intensive degrees to 2-year master's programs, with many offering part-time options and evening classes for working professionals.

name: aisafety.com/funding
current_details: Comprehensive directory of 51 AI safety funding organizations and programs, including grants, fellowships, and fiscal sponsorship opportunities. Covers funders ranging from large-scale philanthropic organizations like Coefficient Giving to specialized programs supporting technical research, governance, journalism, and career transitions. Funding amounts range from $1K to $1M+ with both rolling and deadline-based opportunities across multiple tracks including research grants, rapid grants, and career transition funding.

name: Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship
current_details: The Cooperative AI PhD Fellowship supports PhD students working on multi-agent cooperation and AI safety. Fellows receive annual budgets for conferences, compute, wellbeing, and productivity, plus invitations to CAIF events and collaboration opportunities. CAIF Scholars (top 1% of applicants) receive additional top-up funding of up to $40,000 per year for living expenses, for up to 3 years.

name: Cooperative AI Research Fellowship (Cape Town)
current_details: A full-time 3-month research fellowship for participants from diverse backgrounds to pursue AI safety research from a cooperative AI perspective in Cape Town, South Africa. Fellows receive a $3,000/month stipend, private accommodation in group houses, flights to/from Cape Town, office space with meals, and compute budget. Includes mentorship from top researchers at Google DeepMind, Oxford, and MIT, focusing on multi-agent safety, AI for human cooperation, and mitigating gradual disempowerment.

name: FLI AI Safety PhD Advisor Directory
current_details: A directory of faculty members and AI researchers working on AI existential safety at universities worldwide. Lists professors at institutions like Oxford, UC Berkeley, Stanford, Cambridge, and CMU who are willing to advise students on AI safety research. Also serves as a resource for finding faculty mentors for the Vitalik Buterin postdoctoral and PhD fellowships offered by FLI.

name: PIBBSS x Iliad Research Residency
current_details: The Iliad Fellowship is a 3-month, full-time research fellowship in applied mathematics for AI alignment, targeting PhD or postdoctoral researchers in math, physics, or related fields. Fellows receive a $6,000/month travel-and-housing allowance and work in person at LISA in London (with some remote flexibility for exceptional applicants). The program aims to help fellows develop research proposals and secure philanthropic funding for continued work after the fellowship.

name: Schmidt Sciences AI2050
current_details: AI2050 is a philanthropic initiative of Schmidt Sciences that supports exceptional researchers working on key opportunities and hard problems critical to ensuring AI benefits society. Awards exceptional people as Early Career and Senior Fellows through a nomination-only process, bringing them together into an interdisciplinary community. The 2025 cohort includes 28 scholars receiving $18M+ total in multi-year awards.

name: Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship (FLI)
current_details: The Vitalik Buterin PhD Fellowship in AI Existential Safety supports PhD students working on AI existential safety research. Fellows receive full tuition and fees for 5 years, a $40,000 annual stipend (at US, UK, and Canadian universities), and a $10,000 annual research fund for travel and computing expenses. The fellowship includes invitations to virtual and in-person networking events with other researchers in the field, and applicants who are short-listed receive reimbursement for up to 5 PhD program application fees.

name: AI Policy Leadership Network (APLN)
current_details: Part-time program bringing together approximately 25 experienced AI policy professionals with 6-25 years experience (including 4+ years in AI policy organizations) from government, think tanks, military, intelligence community, and private sector. Features monthly evening discussions in Washington, DC and a multi-day learning trip to the San Francisco Bay Area in April 2026. All expenses covered including travel and accommodations; no stipend provided.

structured.location: Washington, DC & San Francisco Bay Area

name: Americans for Responsible Innovation
current_details: Americans for Responsible Innovation (ARI) is a bipartisan AI policy nonprofit based in Washington, DC that advocates for thoughtful and proactive AI policy frameworks. They offer a referral bonus program of $3,000 for Director/VP level positions and $1,500 for other roles. The careers page currently shows no open positions listed.

name: Career Accelerator (Horizon)
current_details: A 9-month, part-time, remote program to launch your career in AI policy. Participants receive personalized mentorship, application coaching, networking opportunities, and access to exclusive job listings. Can apply for up to $100,000 in flexible funding for internships, upskilling, relocation, and career transitions. Open to applicants from all backgrounds and experience levels—from students and recent graduates to mid-career professionals pivoting into AI policy work.

The program is in-person in Washington, DC and provides direct mentorship from CNAS staff on national security policy issues including defense innovation, economic statecraft, and regional security.

structured.program_dates: Various: June 2026 (Design), September 2026 (Defense, EES), October 2026 (Development), November 2026 (Communications)

name: CSET Summer Internship (Georgetown)
current_details: A 10-week summer internship at Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology focused on emerging technologies (AI, cybersecurity, biotechnology) and national security policy. Designed specifically for students from Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) and other Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs). Interns receive a competitive hourly wage plus living stipend, housing at Georgetown University housing in downtown DC (55 H St NW), and travel reimbursement.

structured.stipend: Competitive hourly wage + living stipend + housing + travel

name: GovAI Summer Fellowship
current_details: Three-month AI governance research fellowship at GovAI in London where participants conduct independent research projects with expert mentorship. Fellows receive a £12,000 stipend plus travel support and weekday lunches, and participate in seminars, Q&A sessions with experts, and networking events. Open to candidates from diverse backgrounds including government, academia, industry, and civil society, from early-career to experienced professionals.

name: Horizon Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - sign up for notifications about future applications
current_details: Fully-funded fellowship placing early-career professionals in Washington, DC policy roles focused on AI, biotechnology, and emerging technologies. Fellows work in executive branch agencies, congressional offices, think tanks, or national laboratories for up to 2 years (1-year renewable terms; 6 months for junior think tank fellows). Competitive compensation: $113K/year for standard fellows or $75K/year for junior fellows, plus $15K health support, $3K professional development stipend, and up to $3K relocation assistance.

structured.duration: Up to 2 years (1-year renewable; 6 months for junior)

name: IAPS AI Policy Fellowship
current_details: The IAPS AI Policy Fellowship is a fully-funded, 3-month program for professionals from varied backgrounds seeking to strengthen practical policy skills for AI governance. Fellows receive $15K (Fellows) or $22K (Senior Fellows) stipends plus travel and accommodation support. The program includes a required 2-week in-person residency in Washington D.C. (June 1-12) with the option to complete remaining time remotely or in D.C., and welcomes international applicants.

name: RAND CAST Fellows
current_deadline: Applications reviewed quarterly: February 1st (response by March 1st), May 1st (response by June 1st), August 1st (response by September 1st), November 1st (response by December 1st)
current_details: The RAND Center on AI, Security, and Technology Fellowship develops policy analysts and implementors at the intersection of technology and security. Fellows perform research in AI Security, Technology Policy and Governance, or Biosecurity, with $40,000–$200,000/year stipends for full-time fellows plus monthly health/dental payments. Fellowships run 6 months to 3 years, can be full- or part-time, and are based in Washington DC, San Francisco, Pittsburgh, remote US locations, or the UK.

structured.location: Washington DC, San Francisco, Pittsburgh, remote US, or UK

name: Tarbell AI Journalism Fellowship
current_deadline: Jan. 7, 2026 (2026 cohort closed); 2027 cohort deadline not yet announced
current_details: One-year journalism fellowship program for journalists interested in covering artificial intelligence. Fellows receive a $60K–$110K stipend (depending on experience and location) and secure a 9-month placement at major newsrooms including Bloomberg, the Guardian, MIT Technology Review, and TIME. Program includes a 10-week remote AI and journalism fundamentals course and a weeklong summit in the San Francisco Bay Area.

structured.location: Remote course + San Francisco Bay Area summit + various newsroom locations

name: Andon Labs — Summer 2026 Role
current_details: Andon Labs is a Y Combinator W24 company building autonomous organizations without humans in the loop. The company is based in San Francisco with a team of 11 people. No job openings are currently posted on the YC platform.

name: ARC Visiting Researcher
current_deadline: Hiring temporarily closed for summer; plans to re-open in September
current_details: Year-round visiting researcher positions at the Alignment Research Center, typically running for ~10 weeks with flexible duration. Most successful candidates have a strong theoretical background in math, physics, or computer science. Most team members join as visiting researchers first to ensure a good fit before considering permanent positions.

name: CAIS Research Engineer Intern (Fall 2026)
current_details: The Center for AI Safety is accepting applications for a Research Engineer Intern position for Fall 2026. CAIS is a leading research and field-building organization focused on reducing societal-scale risks from AI through technical research, field-building initiatives, and policy engagement alongside their sister organization, the CAIS Action Fund.

name: CHAI Internship (UC Berkeley)
current_deadline: Applications for 2026 internships are now closed
current_details: Research internship at UC Berkeley's Center for Human-Compatible Artificial Intelligence for individuals interested in human-compatible AI research, requiring background in machine learning, computer science, mathematics, or related fields. Interns work on supervised research projects, with most producing first-author workshop papers. 12–16 weeks duration with $5,000/month for in-person interns at UC Berkeley or $3,500/month for remote positions.

name: CLR Summer Research Fellowship
current_deadline: Closed - check for next cycle (2027 applications not yet open)
current_details: The Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR) runs an annual 2-month Summer Research Fellowship focused on s-risks (risks of astronomical suffering) and technical AI safety. Fellows work on mentored research projects at CLR's London office, typically held between June and September. The program offers £4,925/month compensation plus professional development and wellbeing budgets, travel and visa support.

name: Constellation Astra Fellowship
current_details: Astra is Constellation's flagship 5-month, fully funded, in-person fellowship at their Berkeley research center that pairs emerging AI safety talent with senior advisors. Fellows receive a $8,400/month stipend, up to $15K/month compute budget for empirical researchers, visa support, and dedicated mentorship on technical research, governance, strategy, and field-building projects. Over 80% of the first cohort transitioned to full-time AI safety roles at organizations like Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepMind, METR, and Redwood Research.

name: DeepMind Student Researcher
current_deadline: Check Google Careers page for specific deadlines by degree level and location
current_details: Paid research internship program for students enrolled in Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD programs to collaborate with leading AI researchers at Google DeepMind, Google Research, and other Google AI teams. Placements run between 12 and 24 weeks with a minimum commitment of four days per week, working in-person at a Google office. Applications are organized by degree level (BS, MS, PhD) and location, with placement across various Google AI teams based on skills and interests.

name: LASR Labs — Summer 2026
current_details: LASR Labs is a 13-week technical AI safety research program in London where participants work in teams of 3-4 with experienced supervisors to produce an academic paper and blog post. Participants receive an £11,000 stipend plus food, office space, and travel support. Alumni have joined UK AISI, Apollo Research, Leap Labs, and Open Philanthropy, and all papers from Summer 2024 were accepted to NeurIPS workshops.

name: OpenAI Emerging Talent
current_details: OpenAI's emerging talent programs include internships, research residencies, and full-time roles designed for people early in their careers with 0–3 years of experience. Programs are available across research, applied engineering, and product areas, welcoming recent graduates and self-taught learners to work on building safe, beneficial AI. Candidates can view open roles and join the Emerging Talent Community for networking opportunities, virtual Q&As, and community events.

name: Tilde Research
current_details: Tilde Research is a mechanistic interpretability lab backed by Khosla Ventures, hiring for multiple technical roles in San Francisco. Positions include ML Researcher, ML Engineer, and Kernel Engineer, all available as both internship and full-time opportunities. All roles are on-site in San Francisco.

name: Virtue AI
current_details: Virtue AI is an AI security and compliance platform founded by Bo Li and Dawn Song. The company offers positions across research, engineering, operations, marketing, and sales in San Francisco, but currently has no open positions listed on their job board.
